context: Re-sync the record at v4 so related_paths and suggested_sweep land in their columns, explicitly retire the 3 hand-mapped evidence rows, verify the finding round-trips losslessly, then delete the file. Do it BEFORE phase 6 so demolition has nothing untracked left to miss, or add the file explicitly to phase 6's deletion list.
description:
_project/blind-spots/2026-07-18-190500-evidence-tree-sha-provenance-mismatch.md is UNTRACKED in git (it exists only in the primary clone's working tree, not in any commit). Phase 6 deletes the tracked _project/blind-spots/*.md records, so a git-based deletion will not necessarily remove this one -- it can silently survive demolition, leaving exactly the kind of stray in-tree findings record the whole domain exists to eliminate (R4).

Its finding IS already landed in production (disposition=open, awaiting triage) and was verified lossless at the time, BUT its related_paths and suggested_sweep were hand-mapped into 3 finding_evidence rows -- the anti-pattern that findings-schema-legacy-frontmatter-mapping-20260724 forbids. Now that v4 has real columns for both, the record should be re-synced from source so its representation matches the pipeline, then the file removed.

Ordering matters and is not obvious: because the source file declares no `evidence:` key, a plain re-sync will NOT clear those 3 rows (parse_draft records evidence_declared, and reconcile only runs when the draft asserts the key -- deliberate, so a legacy record's curated rows are never destroyed). Clearing them is therefore an explicit step, not a side effect of re-syncing.

anti_patterns.dont: Assume phase 6 will remove this file because it lives under _project/blind-spots/
anti_patterns.instead: handle it explicitly here, or add it by name to phase 6's deletion list
anti_patterns.why: it is untracked, so a git-based deletion of tracked records skips it entirely

anti_patterns.dont: Delete the file before its content round-trips losslessly from the v4 columns
anti_patterns.instead: re-sync at v4, verify the round-trip, retire the evidence rows, then delete
anti_patterns.why: the file is the only copy of the original framing, and its DB representation currently uses the forbidden evidence-row fold

preserves.behavior: No content is lost when the hand-mapped evidence rows are retired -- related_paths and suggested_sweep must be in their v4 columns first
The finding's prose stays byte-identical to the source file through the re-sync

verifications.description: the file is gone and the finding still round-trips from its v4 columns
verifications.expected: exit 0; and todo finding show reports related_paths + suggested_sweep from their columns

work_units.evidence: Re-synced the record at v4 (PR #1373 first fixes the prerequisite: there was NO update path for the v4 columns, since related_paths/suggested_sweep sit outside _CONTENT_FIELDS and the reconcile covered only evidence). After the fix, 'todo finding sync' reported 'updated 1' and production now holds related_paths=['_project/audits/todo-db-hosted-acceptance-2026-07-18.md','_project/scripts/audit_sha_check.py'] and the full suggested_sweep string, both verified byte-equal to the source frontmatter.
work_units.summary: Re-sync the record at v4 so related_paths and suggested_sweep land in their columns

NOTE they were removed as a SIDE EFFECT of a second defect found in the same run -- reconcile triggered by another field replaced evidence unconditionally, bypassing the evidence_declared guard. Outcome matches this unit's intent, mechanism was a bug; fixed with a regression test in PR #1373.
work_units.summary: Explicitly retire the 3 hand-mapped finding_evidence rows once their content is in the v4 columns
